svg.title: Fig. 181(b) — A curve with a node: (y² + x² − 3ay)² = 4ay²(2a − y), the sum of a circle and a parabola
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 181(b), page 200. Section: sketching.

g.data-text: The box with its axes, and the equation x = ±√(2ay − y²) ± √(ay): the abscissa is a sum of the abscissa of the circle x² + y² = 2ay and the abscissa of the parabola x² = ay.
Draw the two component curves lightly (dashed): the circle of radius a about (0, a) and the two arms of the parabola x² = ay.
For each y between 0 and 2a add (and subtract) the two abscissae: the four values ±√(2ay − y²) ± √(ay) give the points of the curve on the horizontal through y.
Draw the curve heavy: two big lobes, and a small loop between y = 0 and y = a whose crossing point (0, a) is a node; the lobes touch the x-axis at the origin.
